description: Experience the magic of authentic Indian flavors with our Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, each piece promises a succulent, smoky taste that transports you straight to the streets of Delhi. This recipe ensures perfectly charred edges and a tender, juicy interior, making it an unforgettable dinner.

ingredients.notes: whole chicken cut into 8 pieces or boneless thighs/drumsticks, skin removed

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Make deep gashes on the chicken pieces with a sharp knife. This helps the marinade penetrate the meat effectively.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the gash-cut chicken with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder. Mix well, ensuring chicken is evenly coated. Let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, remaining ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, and the remaining salt. Add mustard oil and a pinch of red food color if desired. Mix thoroughly until smooth.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Add the chicken pieces from the first marinade into the second yogurt mixture. Coat each piece completely, ensuring all surfaces are covered. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor infusion.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Light your charcoal grill and let the coals burn until they are ash-white and emit medium-high heat. Clean the grill grates thoroughly and lightly oil them to prevent the chicken from sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill grates. Grill for 25-35 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through, tender, and has characteristic char marks. Ensure the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes to allow the juices to redistribute. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges, mint chutney, and onion rings.

tips: For maximum flavor and tenderness, marinate the chicken for at least 12-24 hours. The longer the marinade, the deeper the taste and more succulent the chicken will be.

Ensure your charcoal grill is at the right temperature - medium-high heat is crucial for achieving that perfect char without drying out the chicken. Control flare-ups by moving chicken to cooler spots if needed.
Serve Tandoori Chicken hot with a side of cooling mint chutney, sliced onions, and a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice to balance the rich and smoky flavors.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of India right in your backyard with the tantalizing aroma and exquisite flavors of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This iconic Indian dinner recipe, beloved worldwide, reaches its peak of perfection when cooked over hot coals, imparting a smoky depth that an oven simply cannot replicate. Forget restaurant reservations; with a few simple ingredients and a charcoal grill, you can recreate this authentic experience, transforming ordinary chicken into a masterpiece of taste and texture. Get ready to impress your family and friends with a dish that's vibrant, juicy, and bursting with traditional Indian spices.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is more than just a dish; it's a celebration of Punjabi culinary heritage. Traditionally cooked in a cylindrical clay oven known as a tandoor, the chicken is marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices, then skewered and exposed to intense heat. The high temperatures of the tandoor quickly cook the chicken, locking in juices while creating a beautifully charred exterior.

When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're aiming to replicate that signature tandoor experience using a standard charcoal grill. The magic lies in the marinade, which tenderizes the chicken and infuses it with complex flavors like tangy yogurt, pungent ginger-garlic, earthy cumin, fiery chili, and aromatic garam masala. The charcoal grilling method elevates this further, providing an unmistakable smoky essence and a slight crispness to the skin that is utterly irresistible. This process ensures the chicken remains incredibly moist on the inside, with a vibrant red or orange hue on the outside, making it a feast for both the eyes and the palate. It’s a truly authentic way to enjoy this classic Indian dinner recipe.

## Ingredients You Need for Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Crafting the perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken begins with selecting quality ingredients and preparing a robust marinade. Here’s what you’ll need:

-   **For the Chicken:**
    -   2-3 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or breast halves), scored deeply
-   **For the First Marinade:**
    -   1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
    -   1 teaspoon salt
    -   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste (equal parts grated ginger and garlic)
-   **For the Second Marinade (Yogurt Base):**
    -   1 cup full-fat plain yogurt, hung for at least 30 minutes to remove excess water
    -   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
    -   1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat)
    -   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
    -   1 teaspoon cumin powder
    -   1 teaspoon coriander powder
    -   1 teaspoon garam masala
    -   ½ teaspoon black pepper
    -   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
    -   1 tablespoon mustard oil (optional, but highly recommended for authentic flavor)
    -   ½ teaspoon red food coloring (optional, for traditional vibrant color)
    -   Salt to taste
-   **For Grilling:**
    -   Oil or melted butter for basting

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilling Tandoori Chicken

Follow these steps to create an unforgettable Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep gashes or scores into the flesh of the chicken (2-3 per piece) to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply.
2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the lemon juice, salt, and 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste. Rub this mixture all over the scored chicken pieces. Let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes. This step helps tenderize the chicken and kickstarts the flavor infusion.
3.  **Prepare the Second Marinade:** While the chicken rests, prepare the second marinade. In another bowl, combine the hung yogurt, the remaining ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, crushed fenugreek leaves, mustard oil (if using), red food coloring (if using), and salt to taste. Mix everything thoroughly until you have a smooth, thick paste.
4.  **Second Marinade Application:** Add the chicken pieces to the second marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Use your hands to really work the marinade into the scores. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (up to 24 hours) for maximum flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare Your Charcoal Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill for two-zone cooking. Bank the hot coals to one side of the grill for direct high heat, leaving the other side empty for indirect heat. Aim for a medium-high temperature, around 375-400°F (190-200°C). Clean your grill grates and lightly oil them.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Remove the chicken from the fridge about 30 minutes before grilling to bring it closer to room temperature.
    -   Place the chicken pieces directly over the hot coals for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char and sear. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
    -   Once lightly charred, move the chicken to the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the lid to allow the chicken to cook through evenly.
    -   Cook for 20-30 minutes, turning occasionally, until the internal temperature of the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) on an instant-read thermometer.
    -   During the last 5-10 minutes of cooking, you can baste the chicken with a little oil or melted butter to keep it moist and enhance browning.
7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a tender and moist result.

## Pro Tips for the Best Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Achieving restaurant-quality Tandoori Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tricks:

-   **Deep Scoring is Key:** Don't be shy with scoring the chicken. Deeper cuts allow the marinade to penetrate more effectively, leading to more flavorful and tender chicken.
-   **Hung Yogurt Makes a Difference:** Straining your yogurt removes excess water, resulting in a thicker marinade that clings better to the chicken, preventing it from sliding off during grilling.
-   **Marination Time is Crucial:** While 4 hours is the minimum, marinating overnight (12-24 hours) yields significantly more tender and flavorful chicken. Plan ahead for the best results.
-   **Master Two-Zone Grilling:** This technique is essential for Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. The initial direct heat creates beautiful char marks, while indirect heat ensures the chicken cooks through without burning on the outside.
-   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** Overcooked chicken is dry chicken. An instant-read thermometer is your best friend to ensure the chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) without going beyond.
-   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Giving each piece enough space on the grill promotes even cooking and better charring.
-   **Baste for Moisture and Shine:** A light basting with oil or melted butter towards the end of cooking adds moisture, flavor, and that desirable glossy finish.
-   **Choose Quality Charcoal:** Hardwood lump charcoal burns hotter and imparts a cleaner, more natural smoky flavor compared to briquettes.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

Tandoori Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a range of accompaniments, making it a perfect centerpiece for any Indian dinner recipe spread.

-   **Classic Pairings:** Serve hot off the grill with fresh lemon wedges, a sprinkle of chopped cilantro, and thinly sliced red onion rings.
-   **Bread:** Warm naan bread, roti, or paratha are excellent for scooping up the chicken and its delicious juices.
-   **Rice:** A side of fragrant basmati rice, jeera rice (cumin rice), or a simple pilaf complements the rich flavors.
-   **Dips and Sauces:** A cooling mint chutney or a refreshing raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and spices) provides a wonderful contrast to the spicy chicken.
-   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion, and cilantro with a lemon dressing) adds freshness and crunch.
-   **Beverages:** Pair with a traditional mango lassi, a cold Indian beer, or even a crisp white wine.

## Variations and Substitutions for Tandoori Chicken

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a culinary delight, don't hesitate to experiment with variations:

-   **Other Proteins:** The tandoori marinade is incredibly versatile. Try it with paneer (Indian cheese) for Tandoori Paneer, fish fillets for Tandoori Fish, or even large shrimp for Tandoori Shrimp. You can also use it for vegetables like bell peppers, onions, and cauliflower.
-   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder or add a touch of cayenne pepper for more heat. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder.
-   **Flavor Enhancements:** A pinch of smoked paprika can enhance the smoky flavor, especially if you're not using charcoal. A touch of honey or brown sugar in the marinade can add a subtle sweetness and help with caramelization.
-   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** If a charcoal grill isn't an option, you can still make Tandoori Chicken:
    -   **Oven:** Preheat your oven to its highest setting (usually 450-500°F / 230-260°C). Place chicken on a rack over a baking sheet and bake for 20-30 minutes, flipping halfway, or until cooked through and lightly charred. For extra char, finish under the broiler for a few minutes.
    -   **Gas Grill:** Use a gas grill with a two-zone setup. For added smoky flavor, you can place a foil packet of wood chips (soaked in water) directly over one of the burners.
    -   **Air Fryer:** For smaller batches, an air fryer can achieve good results at 375-400°F (190-200°C), cooking for 15-25 minutes, flipping halfway.

Whichever method you choose, the essence of the marinade will shine through, but for that truly authentic, deep smoky flavor, nothing beats the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken.

Bringing the authentic taste of India to your home kitchen has never been easier or more rewarding. This Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is more than just an Indian dinner recipe; it's an experience that tantalizes all your senses. The rich aroma of spices mingling with the smoky char, the vibrant colors, and the incredibly tender, juicy chicken will transport you straight to the bustling streets of Punjab. So fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and prepare to create a culinary masterpiece that will have everyone asking for seconds. Enjoy the magic of homemade tandoori!
